The calibration directory is small and well-described, with wiki/code/math/dialogue hashes plus refusal/benign metadata and newer 400k-character agent-domain variants.

cards.name: Attention tree pruning relevance to Cerebellum
cards.description:
**Question:**
Is tree-based top-k attention pruning relevant to Cerebellum quality research, or only an inference-speed side note?

**Current belief:**
Probably not a core Cerebellum issue; relevance is unclear and speculative unless quantization changes attention spikiness.

**Test plan:**
Do nothing unless an experiment can measure whether Cerebellum quantization changes attention spikiness enough to affect pruning power.

**Decision rule:**
Archive if no concrete quant-quality interaction is found; keep in intake only as a watch item for future inference work.

**Evidence:**
- `research/external/attention_tree_pruning.md`: Summarizes pruning as inference-speed work, not quantization-quality work, with only a speculative spikiness interaction.
- `docs/multi_domain_ablation.md`: Project goal is smaller without being dumber via mixed precision, so speed-only ideas need a clear quality or fit connection.

cards.name: Gemma 4 block-10 hillstep regressed HumanEval despite lower wiki PPL
cards.description:
**Question:**
Should the exhaustive wiki-only block-10 hillstep path be retired or kept only as forensic data?

**Current belief:**
Do not resume it as-is. The checkpoint improved wiki PPL from 2504.2787 to 1615.8505, but HumanEval+ fell from 83.54 to 69.51, size grew by 1.02 GiB, and throughput dropped by roughly 7.5-8 tok/s.

**Test plan:**
Keep the frozen checkpoint only for comparison. Rebuild protected variants from the same lock map with early blocks, attention, and Q2 ffn_up/ffn_gate restored to safer floors, then run HumanEval+ chat, ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU-Redux, PPL, size, and TPS.

**Decision rule:**
Archive the path if protected rebuilds recover HumanEval+ while retaining acceptable PPL/size; never publish or resume the block-10 checkpoint unless it clears the full benchmark gate against Q4_K_M.

**Evidence:**
- `/var/home/deucebucket/games/cerebellum-runs/families/gemma-4/gemma-4-12b-it/sources/google-f16/runs/gemma4-12b-cerebellum-q4km-wiki-visible-20260604/benchmarks/block10_vs_q4/COMPARISON_SUMMARY.json`: Decision says not to resume this exhaustive wiki-only path; records benchmark deltas, size, TPS, and PPL.

cards.description:
**Question:**
Can the Python 18K LoRA improve coding on top of Gemma 4 26B without breaking the v6 Cerebellum precision map?

**Current belief:**
The LoRA adapter targets q/k/v/o plus gate/up/down projections with rank 32 and was trained on Python Code Instructions 18K. It is likely relevant to Codex/coding work, but adapter merge changes the base weights and may invalidate the existing v6 tensor sensitivities.

**Test plan:**
Merge the adapter into a scratch BF16 model, generate a Q4_K_M baseline and a v6-transfer quant, then run HumanEval+ chat and Python-focused smoke prompts.

**Decision rule:**
Proceed only if merged LoRA beats v6 on coding tasks after anti-misgrade audit and does not materially regress ARC/HellaSwag smoke.

**Evidence:**
